gluttonous

GLUT-uh-nus · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Gluttonous is excessively greedy in eating or drinking.

The gluttonous puppy ate its own dinner, then finished the cat's food before anyone noticed.

Example

At the buffet, the gluttonous diner returned for a fifth plate before most guests had finished their first.

Gluttonous describes excessive, often uncontrolled eating or consumption, usually with a disapproving tone.

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

greedy: Greedy means wanting far more of something than you need -- food, money, or attention. Gluttonous narrows that greed to one arena, eating and drinking: every gluttonous feast is greedy, but a greedy person might hoard money while barely touching food.

ravenous: Ravenous means so hungry that you are desperate to eat right now -- an intense need of the moment. Gluttonous is not about need at all: a gluttonous eater keeps going long after the hunger is gone, out of habit and excess.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

abstemious: moderate in eating and drinking

moderate: not excessive or extreme

Where it sits · how far past need the eating goes

hungry → gluttonous → insatiable

hungry vs. gluttonous: Hungry simply describes wanting food; gluttonous implies eating far past the point of need, to excess.

insatiable vs. gluttonous: Insatiable pushes past even gluttonous: a gluttonous eater takes far more than they need, but an insatiable appetite can never be satisfied at all, no matter how much it is given.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — glutt: to swallow (Latin (gluttire))

suffix — -onous: full of, characterized by (Latin)

Put it together: glutt- ('to swallow') + -onous together describe someone who swallows food excessively.

Use the root in a new word: glutton: Glutton is the noun form of the same word family, naming the excessively greedy eater directly.
